record_notes.DCP-LETT-1546: A two-page manuscript memorandum, forwarded by Hooker, headed Most Anomalous Leguminosae (from Bentham), with 21 named genera and species counts. It is not Darwin prose or a one-page complete letter. The specific family and list fulfil 1612 P4 request, corroborated by the source footnote. Retain after December 11, 1854 and the original December 12–31 XML bounds; no exact day or Darwin receipt is known. No omitted list items are invented.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1612: Monday 11, supplied December 1854. P1–4 answer 1611 encouragement, Aquilegia proof, sampling cautions, anomaly objection and Australia question, while P2 explicitly contrasts the earlier 1607 disruption sentence with 1611 second letter. This is a joint-input response, not two independent full answers. Returning the proof establishes reading by December 11, not Hooker receipt. Darwin explains extinction and rarity using ornithorhynchus, Echidna, marsupials, Sagitta and earwig, explicitly fears circularity, and asks for Bentham Leguminosae data. P5 Forbes memorial subscription is a wish, not paid. P7 duck weights and P8–14 subsequent tabulation are further work; raw 17th, diag/ramme and 15.05 must not be silently normalized to a guessed fraction or earlier 15.07. Later Natural Selection, Origin, Variation and Expression quotations in apparatus are not this letter or contemporary retrieved writings.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1638: Incoming fragment before March 7, 1855; original XML lower bound is broad 1809, not proof of early composition. Read afresh although accepted prior readings exist. Hooker seeks Godron after having read it since his return from India; he has not yet found or supplied it. He cautions that naturalised plant categories and individual species require scrutiny, reports Tasmanian/Australian alpine correspondences and Swan River distinctness, returns from Thomson marriage, arranges Linnean borrowing through Bennett and advocates the new journal. Ending is missing. Godron, Australian Alps, colonist tabulation, Bennett and journal are specifically answered in 1643. Brown-crayon marks are undated; later publication and library possession are not a dated reading of Godron by Darwin.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1643: March 7 with supplied 1855 year. P1–7 explicitly answer 1638 Godron search, geographical sketch, Australian Alps, colonist tabulation, Bennett borrowing and Linnean journal. Two Godron notes to Darwin and two to Lindley are mentioned; only one incoming fragment is identified. Atlas study does not prove the missing atlas text of 1641 had now arrived. P4 asks for Gray and Flora Cestrica, not receipt. P8 Huxley memoir question comes from missing incoming material. P9–11 separately report finished work on Wollaston book and four Atlantis assumptions from correspondence: the specific assumptions in 1640 P11–13 prove reading of that source by March 7. Publication/gift slip dated March 10 does not date the earlier reading. No Waterhouse tarsal memorandum is mentioned.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1644: Incoming fragment before March 17, 1855, read afresh. P1 starts within a discussion of Bunbury/Ophrys and competing migration/creation explanations. P2–3 and P9 directly engage Darwin winglessness hypothesis in 1643, with Kerguelen, desert counterexamples and a proposed test of European species. P4 offers library workarounds after Kippist refusal; P5 promises the requested two books; P6 explicitly responds to Johnston atlas and overlapping circles; none of these promises establishes delivery. P7–8 add completed Australian Leguminosae catalogue and strong endemism/sameness distinctions. The March 17 Darwin note is quoted in full in footnote 4 and witnesses Kerguelen/desert/wing questions by then. Ink and pencil annotations are separately undated. Response to March 7 bounds composition no earlier than March 7 and original upper bound remains March 16; no exact day selected.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1661: April 7 with supplied 1855 year begins seed-salting inquiry after an earlier in-person meeting. The morning Rhododendron thank-you note is missing. Darwin asks for easily available susceptible seeds and expected survival times, consults Lindley on albumen, and recalls an old coal-plant disagreement. P7 reports Davy salmon-ova survival and paper submission; this is a report to Hooker, not a direct response to an identified Hooker letter. The North American lady/Ditiscus recollection is a separate uncertain report, not already verified fish ova transport. Later June correspondence in a footnote must not be treated as an April prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1667: April 13 with supplied 1855 year, written BY Darwin. Requests a list of twelve superior Royal Society candidates; he is not supplying that list here. Asks to borrow an old Lawsonian synopsis because purchase failed and explains intended erasable marks. Berkeley peas received; forty-five varieties are planned together. He doubts the lady water-bug ova story without better information. P4 replies to a missing Hooker seed note, declines the suggested scale, reports one-week success and varied germination rather than universal survival, and plants the fourteen-day batch today. Temperature and flow calculations are historical claims. P5 sends his Gray naturalised-plant list for advice and describes masking names before selection to avoid bias; enclosed list is not transcribed here. P7 records unsalted comparison and glass tumblers. Old March library/winglessness letters are not the missing seed response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1669: April 19 with supplied 1855 year, written BY Darwin, not Hooker. P1 thanks for a missing Royal Society candidate list, naturally following Darwin April 13 request but not a reply to his own letter. P2 responds to missing seed advice, declines immense scale, rejects cambric packets because of trapped air, proposes 40–50 bottles and seeks marked lists. P3 reports Berkeley Margate experiment from a letter received today and explicitly disclaims offence. P4 distinguishes fourteen-day outcomes, dead cabbage, delayed/damaged radish and vigorous cress; other seeds have seven-day results. P7 still awaits advice on Gray list. Printed seed catalogues are only possibly identified by editors, and there is no evidence Hooker marked them.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1671: April 24 with supplied 1855 year thanks Sir William through Joseph for a gift, explicitly contrasted with the originally requested loan; not merely a loan acknowledgement. Identification as Lawsonian synopsis is editorially probable. A missing Hooker question asks whether seeds float: all sink after hours except beet, with shaking to encourage sinking. Hooker expectation of death after a week is reported but the underlying note is missing. Darwin reports cress/lettuce germination after twenty-one days and postpones a further experiment because of cold ground. The seeds-already-reached-islands argument is from another unidentified letter, not Hooker by default. A separate April 13 experimental note quoted by editors cannot be silently merged with April 24 composition.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1680: May 11 with supplied 1855 year, Darwin to Hooker. Explicitly received note just now brings assistant-director appointment news, not the later directorship itself. Salary and expected promotion are qualified; he promises discretion. A missing note also asks about Job, publication venue, Kerguelen insects and club matters. Westminster article location and proposed loan are separate from modern attribution to Froude. Seed report to Lindley is planned and later permanent publication conditional; May 26 and 1856 publications are later events. The two-sex moth detail is absent from 1644, so P4 is not uniquely a delayed reply to that older source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1681: May 15, supplied month/year from fish experiment evidence, Darwin to Hooker, not an incoming Hooker response. Two Hooker notes and Scoresby dry but useful answer are unlocated. The MathML in P2 is 1/2 hour, not twelve hours talking to Sabine. P3 imagined fish/heron transport fails when the fish eject the seeds; do not train imagined success as observed result. P4 future fresh-seed and pod/branch flotation trials are prospective; later May 17 note cannot be projected into May 15. P5–6 and P9 request Mimosa/Guillandina and Lofoten seed trials, distinguish Robert Brown report and Keeling recollection, and end with 1000-to-1 doubt. P7 criticises De La Rue exclusion while praising his council conduct. Same-author 1680 is not its incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1640: March 2 with supplied 1855 year; complete twelve-page Wollaston letter, seventeen body blocks, read with all marginalia, footnotes and bibliography. A missing Darwin query arrived February 27; that is Wollaston receipt, not Darwin receipt of this reply. Ten answers cover possible Zargus/Calathus hybrid and damaged specimen, Dezerta geography/cultivation, Salvages sample uncertainty, widespread versus locally abundant insects, transitional families, variation, wings and Atlantis. Contrary to the Luna probe, P6 EXPLICITLY discusses five-jointed tarsi, Tomicidae and Anisotomidae; Waterhouse 1625 is a relevant comparison, but no Darwin use of that later memorandum is established. P8 permits adaptive wing change within fixed species limits, not endorsement of transmutation; P10 admits no measured same-island wing range. P11–13 explicitly state the four assumptions Darwin criticises in 1643. P14 distinguishes introduced winged and indigenous flightless species. Departure dates are alternatives, not realised travel. Later gift slip and hostile Origin review are separate apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1609: Explicit accepted primary source/body reading reused with matching pins. December 2 with supplied 1854 year. P1 distinguishes Darwin attendance at the medal presentation from second-hand praise of Hooker dinner speech; he did not hear that speech himself. P2 reports breakfast the next morning. P3 explicitly acknowledges both aberrant genera and Australian geography from 1607 but says he has not had time to consider them; that narrow acknowledgement is a direct response. Preserve the separate earlier dated notes in 1607 apparatus rather than flattening all consideration into one event. P5 sends to Hooker father because the Richmond address is unknown, not a new incoming address letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1610: Explicit accepted primary source/body reading reused with matching pins. December 4 with supplied 1854 year. P1–3 directly engage the Bentham list and distinctive Australia-splitting speculation in 1607, including concern that selecting only small genera biases the result. Darwin asks Hooker to query Bentham, discusses genus/family equivalence and withholds trust in the list. These are definite content matches, not merely adjacent letters. P4–5 asks for evidence/publication of Aquilegia unity from an earlier remark not preserved here. P6 reports reading Forbes tribute in Gardeners Chronicle; P7 hopes the move is comfortable, and P9 describes difficulty renting a London house. Later successful January tenancy is not December knowledge. Accept P1–3 as the response section; later independent topics remain separate grounding.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1611: Explicit accepted primary source/body reading reused with matching pins. December 5 with supplied 1854 year; incomplete incoming letter ends mid-sentence. Hooker answers the December 4 questions specifically, reports seeing Bentham today, distinguishes size alone from size plus natural-order status, warns about memorable large genera in a miscellaneous sample, argues rarity and anomaly may be circular, and suggests single-order comparisons. P4 quotes Darwin objection about splitting Australia and asks two alternative meanings. P5 sends unpublished Aquilegia results, explains imperfect proof and requests return; later publication and promised copy are not already received. The attached Darwin memorandum, later ink/pencil comments, and later Natural Selection quotations are not Hooker letter voice or automatically dated December 5. No Darwin receipt date is established by this reverse reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1607: Explicit accepted primary source/body reading reused with matching pins. Wednesday is original; November 15, 1854 is inferred from a November 20 Darwin note, whose content is only described in the editorial footnote. Hooker says 80 anomalous genera but only 40 rows survive, as the footnote explicitly notes. The two counts are Steudel versus Hooker/Bentham estimates. P2 develops the distinct longitudinal Australia-split, climate, extinction and new-creation argument, with hypothetical assumptions retained. The request was already pending in 1629/1600, not uniquely identifiable with same-day 1601. Read all 40 rows and later Darwin notes: pinned November 30 note is dated; the additional calculation and pencil annotations are not assigned the incoming date. Raw HTML has literal totals 1161 1132 and MathML numerator 6722 / denominator 78005; the quoted footnote calculation claims 11.6. These are source rendering inconsistencies requiring later verification, not permission to invert fractions, remove leading digits or invent 40 missing rows. No inline figure exists.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1625: Explicit accepted primary source/body reading reused with matching pins. Waterhouse memorandum dated after March 2, 1855 from a Wollaston exchange, with raw year-end bound; no exact March day chosen. Full list covers tarsal counts and sex differences in Anisotomidae, Cryptophagidae, Mycetophagidae and Staphylinidae, with continuations and ditto marks tied to their correct rows. Male/female symbols and counts are substantive. Raw diag/ramme debris and flattened layout are retained in the source projection. Darwin separate note, later chapter label and Origin quotations must not inherit the memorandum date or Waterhouse voice. The bibliographic entry under Wollaston does not itself authenticate the relevant letter or book. This tarsal list is not the missing atlas text discussed in 1641.

reading_method: All eleven targets and additional Wollaston 1640 independently read in full, including all source apparatus. The initially truncated middle of 1640 was separately read in full. Five prior source/body readings reused with matching accepted note, ledger and source pins. MathML 1681 and literal 1612 weight expression inspected directly. No new inline figures.
